[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cddjz1r01l8o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
Nirmal Purja at the summit of Mount Everest

A ten-member international mountaineering team led by renowned Nepal-born former Royal Marine Nirmal Purja is feared missing after an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak, one of the world's highest mountains.

Pakistani mountaineering officials say the avalanche hit at around midday on Thursday on the 8,047-metre (26,400 ft) peak in the Karakoram range. There has been no subsequent communication with the team.

An American, a Chinese national, an Omani and five Nepalis are said to be part of the climbing group.

Purja, the expedition leader, is known for climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre plus mountains in just over six months in 2019.

"We are coordinating with the authorities and trying to arrange a helicopter rescue on Friday morning Pakistani time depending on weather condition," Karrar Haidri, the vice-president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan told the BBC.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for expeditions, and is ranked as the world's 12th highest peak.

In a separate statement, the Alpine Club of Pakistan said it had been "in constant contact" with the authorities to ensure that "all available resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity".

"The Club prays for the safety and successful rescue of all the climbers and stands in solidarity with their families and the international mountaineering community during this difficult time," it added.

Purja joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009.

His climbing career began when he walked to Everest base camp in 2012 and, instead of returning as planned, decided to climb the entire mountain.

President of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, Major General Irfan Arshad, said its leaders were in close contact with government officials to assist with the ongoing search and rescue operation.

Arshad said the club was making every effort to send helicopters and other available relief resources to the area as soon as possible.

As per Outside Magazine: "Tracking data of the expedition shows a rapid descent that would align with that of an avalanche.

"Rescue efforts are underway, but are not expected to reach the mountain until Friday morning (local time)." As per time of writing, it is 5.25am locally, or 1.25am BST.

Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world.

It stands at an elevation of 8,051 meters (26,414 feet) above sea level and is considered one of the most difficult peaks tackled by climbers.

An avalanche struck an expedition on Broad Peak (8,047m) in Pakistan's Karakoram mountain range around midday on Thursday, July 30, leaving a team of 10 climbers missing.

Among those caught in the avalanche is renowned Nepalese mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja MBE – widely known as Nimsdai – a former British special forces soldier and one of the world's most accomplished high-altitude climbers.

Purja served for 16 years in the British military, including 10 years with UK Special Forces after becoming the first Gurkha to pass the elite SBS selection process. He later achieved global recognition by climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre peaks in a record six months and six days, a feat documented in the Netflix film 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible.

In 2018, he was awarded an MBE by Queen Elizabeth II for his exceptional military service in high-risk environments.

The summer climbing season in Pakistan’s Karakoram Mountains has taken a tragic turn after a massive avalanche on the 26,400-foot-tall Broad Peak has left ten climbers missing, including Nirmal “Nims” Purja.

According to a press release posted on the Alpine Club of Pakistan’s Instagram channel, the avalanche struck a group of climbers climbing Broad Peak around midday on Thursday, July 30. “The entire team has been out of communication since the avalanche,” the statement reads.

Tracking data of the expedition shows a rapid descent that would align with that of an avalanche.

Rescue efforts are underway, but are not expected to reach the mountain until Friday morning local time.

Purja was leading an expedition for his company, Elite Exped, when the avalanche occurred. Purja rose to fame after the popular Netflix documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible was released in 2021, chronicling his successful attempt to break the previous speed record for climbing the world’s 14 peaks above 8,000 meters. His career has been defined by success and controversy, including allegations of sexual assault during expeditions, as reported by The New York Times.

According to the Everest Chronicle, the avalanche occurred only days after Nims completed his 57th successful ascent of an 8,000-meter peak with an oxygenless ascent of Gasherbrum II on July 21. He was nearing completion of his Hat Trick Campaign to climb all 14 8,000-meter peaks three times. Purja is also known for his foundation, which raised funds to give back to the mountaineering community....
